mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES from -8.3 to -37.0 will reduce commuter-linked retail visits after a short lag, so RETAIL_REC will fall further over the next month unless workplace mobility rebounds quickly.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 and TRANSIT falls below -25 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above its prior 28-day mean despite WORKPLACES staying below -20 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM indicates routine, necessity-based trips that crowd out discretionary shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC weaker over the next 1 to 2 weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the last 4 weeks when GROCERY_PHARM remains above 0 for two successive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT stays depressed after the current plunge, access to malls and shopping districts will remain constrained and RETAIL_REC will move lower within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by at least 5 points week-on-week from an already sub -20 level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT remains below -20 and WORKPLACES remains below -15.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS signals more outdoor leisure and family outings, which can spill over into nearby retail and recreation trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week from a negative baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve relative to the last 4 weeks after PARKS increases for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, home-centered activity substitutes for shopping trips and RETAIL_REC declines over the following month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 10 and WORKPLACES staying below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A reopening regime that lifts WORKPLACES and TRANSIT together will restore weekday footfall and push RETAIL_REC higher within four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 10 points from its current week and TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its prior 4-week mean even after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The recent jump in GROCERY_PHARM from -1.1 to 9.7 is a threshold marker for precautionary or household stock-up behavior, which diverts spending from discretionary retail and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 5 after a prior week below 5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week of GROCERY_PHARM crossing above 5.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS remain less negative while RESIDENTIAL also stays elevated, people are spending more time locally and the extra neighborhood activity will support retail visits over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by at least 5 points while RESIDENTIAL stays above 15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise relative to the prior 28 days after PARKS improves and RESIDENTIAL remains above 15 for two consecutive weeks.
